items.label: f04-ai-timeout-honest
items.front: What happens now when the AI analysis never arrives (after 6 polls)?
items.back: The estimator sets aiStatus 'degraded', pushes an estimator_ai_timeout event and shows the summary as a preliminary estimate. Previously it silently showed the local baseline, indistinguishable from a real analysis (HN-06).

items.label: f02-fail-open-rate-limit
items.front: Why the old in-memory rate limiter was wrong on Lambda, and why the new one fails open
items.back: A module-scoped Map starts empty on every cold start, so concurrent instances made the advertised 5-per-15-minutes limit unenforced, and a module-level setInterval kept timers alive. The store is now pluggable (DynamoDB with TTL). If the store is down the request is allowed: abuse prevention must not become an outage that loses real leads.

items.label: f01-plasmic-two-rules
items.front: The two Plasmic rules in HyperNova
items.back: 1) Never edit anything under components/plasmic/: it is regenerated on every design sync. 2) All behaviour goes in the hand-written wrapper (e.g. components/ContactForm.tsx), which passes the generated component overrides, slot content and variants.

items.label: f03-pre-commit-add-all
items.front: What is surprising about this repo's pre-commit hook?
items.back: It runs npm run lint and then `git add -A` if anything is unstaged, so it stages everything in your working tree, including files you deliberately left out of the commit.

items.prompt: A teammate committed and pushed an API token, then deleted the file in the next commit. What is the first thing to do?

choices.text: Rotate the credential
Nothing more: deleting the file in the next commit removed the secret
Rewrite the history with git filter-repo and force-push every branch
Add the file to .gitignore so the token cannot be committed again

choices: Rotate the credential
Nothing more: deleting the file in the next commit removed the secret
Rewrite the history with git filter-repo and force-push every branch
Add the file to .gitignore so the token cannot be committed again

items.explanation: Deleting the file does not remove the secret: it is still in the history of every clone and fork. Until the old value is revoked nothing else matters; untracking, ignoring and optional history rewriting come after.

items.prompt: As inherited, the estimator subscribed to onUpdateProject without variables and checked the id in the browser. What was actually wrong with that?

choices.text: It made the AI enrichment worker process each submitted project twice
Every visitor's browser received every other visitor's project updates
Nothing beyond wasted bandwidth, since mismatched updates were discarded
Missed own updates

choices: It made the AI enrichment worker process each submitted project twice
Every visitor's browser received every other visitor's project updates
Nothing beyond wasted bandwidth, since mismatched updates were discarded
Missed own updates

items.explanation: Without variables AppSync pushed every project update to every connected client; the client-side id check hid a data leak instead of preventing it. The fix passes filter: { id: { eq: projectId } } and keeps the client check as defence in depth (HN-10).
